plan.question: Does the aligned unit-normalized, half-tangent backbone retain its improvement over the original target-aware reference across prospectively fixed paired seeds, and does complete-row magnitude rescaling add a reproducible incremental benefit? The observed limitation is unsupported selection from a historical maximum: latest frozen magnitude/control AUCs are 0.6149336526209208/0.6151021885074872 (delta -0.00016853588656640106), with Logloss delta +0.00006131347503079976 on 3,234,051 validation impressions. Both runs succeeded with equal parameter counts. The control matches r0012-scale_half and exceeds baseline-din by 0.0017402023884189 AUC at declared seed42; this is same-seed evidence for accumulated changes, not independent-seed robustness or single-component attribution. Preserve the round26 magnitude gain of 0.000024328076400625953 and historical round17 maximum, alongside its adverse exact-source replay and the differing same-source round23 results. Retrieve the complete recent scoped interpretations, alternatives, failed trajectories and resource caveats to prepare a minimal frozen comparison, using the control as the current anchor. Conditional on a later authorized interface, compare fixed sources at paired seeds42/43/44 against the original reference and necessary normalization/projection controls, recording all signed outcomes and costs. Mixed or negative incremental effects, or execution spread comparable to the benefit, would leave a robust magnitude advantage unsupported; lost backbone gains would weaken its robustness claim. Neither favorable performance nor bounded gradient diagnostics establishes semantic conflict resolution or aggregation-to-final-score mediation. No further adaptive seed42 probe or architecture sweep is justified by the current evidence and inherited reserve. This query phase admits no experiment and makes no final selection or withheld request.
